title: Fulvestrant · injections every 4 weeks
context_label: Postmenopausal ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer
schedule_summary: NCCP schedule: 500 mg on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of each 28-day cycle. This means Day 29 next, then every 28 days.
purpose: The aim is to control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer and its symptoms, with response and tolerability reviewed before continuing.
indication_text: This NCCP monotherapy pathway covers postmenopausal women with ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has relapsed or progressed on or after adjuvant anti-oestrogen treatment. Fulvestrant prescribed with capivasertib or a CDK4/6 medicine follows a separate combination regimen.
administration_text: Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.
monitoring_summary: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, the menopausal and treatment history, pregnancy exclusion and bleeding risk. Before injections, tell staff about anticoagulants, bruising, bleeding or previous nerve symptoms. Repeat liver tests when indicated; scans follow the agreed cancer-control plan. Tell anyone ordering an oestrogen blood test that you receive fulvestrant because some tests can give a misleadingly high result.
review_status: Source reconciled; independent clinical, pharmacy and patient/PPI review pending

agents.name: Fulvestrant
agents.mechanism: Binds the oestrogen receptor, blocks its signalling and helps the cell remove the receptor
visual: Oestrogen receptors can drive cancer-cell growth
Fulvestrant binds and blocks the receptor
The number of receptors falls, reducing growth signals
agents.explanation: Fulvestrant is a selective oestrogen-receptor degrader. It blocks receptor activity and lowers the amount of receptor available in cancer cells. The slow-release injection keeps the medicine in the body between visits; the extra first-month dose helps establish treatment exposure.
agents.watch: Report severe injection pain, numbness, weakness or pain travelling down the leg, unusual bleeding or bruising, jaundice and symptoms that interfere with daily life.
risks: Injection-site pain and uncommon nerve injury
Liver enzyme changes or liver injury
Bleeding / bruising risk with intramuscular injections

urgent_extra: Tell the team about unusual bleeding or extensive bruising, injection-site pain with numbness or pain down the leg, jaundice or worsening symptoms. Severe chest pain, breathlessness or stroke symptoms require emergency help.

sections.title: The first month is different
sections.text: There is an extra injection visit two weeks after the first dose. After the Day 29 dose, visits continue every 28 days. Ask the team to confirm each appointment.

sections.title: Before an injection
sections.text: Tell staff about anticoagulants, unusual bleeding or bruising. Do not stop an anticoagulant yourself. The team reviews injection safety and any dose modification.

sections.title: Injection technique and aftercare
sections.text: Staff give deep intramuscular gluteal injections slowly. Report severe pain, numbness or pain radiating down the leg promptly.

sections.title: If a visit is delayed
sections.text: Contact the clinic to agree the next date. Do not calculate a catch-up or extra dose from this reference graphic; dose scheduling remains the clinical team’s responsibility.

sections.title: Other cancer medicines
sections.text: If you also receive capivasertib or a CDK4/6 medicine, use the full combination plan for tablets, safety checks and side-effect advice. Fulvestrant-alone information cannot replace it.

sections.title: Oestrogen blood tests
sections.text: Tell the clinician and laboratory that you receive fulvestrant. Some antibody-based tests can read falsely high; the team should confirm how a result was measured before changing treatment.

evidence.title: Why fulvestrant is offered
evidence.population: Postmenopausal people with hormone-sensitive advanced breast cancer studied in endocrine-treatment trials.
evidence.primary_endpoint: Control of cancer progression and survival, evaluated separately.
evidence.interpretation: Fulvestrant can help control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer. Studies support the usual treatment schedule, while the choice of treatment depends on previous endocrine therapy and the individual cancer.
evidence.limitations: A study comparing fulvestrant doses does not show that monotherapy is better than modern combination treatment. A separate study in people who had not received endocrine therapy found longer control of progression but no proven overall-survival advantage over anastrozole. These findings do not predict an individual outcome.
evidence.intro: Fulvestrant can help control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer. Studies support the usual treatment schedule, while the choice of treatment depends on previous endocrine therapy and the individual cancer.

consent_support: Discuss the treatment aim, injection discomfort and possible nerve injury, bleeding or bruising, liver effects, flushes, joint symptoms and fatigue. Liver impairment or an existing modified dose requires an agreed prescriber and pharmacy plan. Where relevant, use effective contraception during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded. Tell staff about blood thinners; do not stop them yourself.

support.title: Make injection visits manageable
support.text: Discuss injection discomfort, flushes, joint or muscle symptoms, fatigue and nausea. Ask early for symptom help or practical support attending appointments.

support.title: Support medicines
support.text: Fulvestrant alone does not require routine steroid premedication, injections to raise white cells or a standard anti-sickness course. A combination medicine can add its own supportive-care needs.

support.title: Bleeding and nerve symptoms
support.text: Tell staff about blood thinners, unusual bruising or bleeding before an injection. Severe buttock pain, new numbness, weakness or pain down the leg needs prompt assessment.

support.title: Tests and appointments
support.text: Confirm the extra loading visit and later appointments, who books required blood tests and scans, and who reviews the results. Tell the laboratory team about fulvestrant if an oestrogen blood test is ordered.

chapters.title: The treatment being discussed
chapters.intro: The aim is to control advanced hormone-sensitive breast cancer and its symptoms, with response and tolerability reviewed before continuing.

items.title: Who this information covers
items.text: This NCCP monotherapy pathway covers postmenopausal women with ER-positive locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer that has relapsed or progressed on or after adjuvant anti-oestrogen treatment. Fulvestrant prescribed with capivasertib or a CDK4/6 medicine follows a separate combination regimen.

items.title: Medicine and schedule
items.text: NCCP schedule: 500 mg on Days 1 and 15 of the first 28-day cycle, then Day 1 of each 28-day cycle. This means Day 29 next, then every 28 days. Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself.

items.title: Review and duration
items.text: Each usual 500 mg dose is given as two 5 mL injections, one in each buttock, slowly over one to two minutes per injection. This is not an intravenous infusion; no port or pump is needed for fulvestrant itself. Symptoms can occur at any time; this is not a chemotherapy nadir or recovery curve.

items.title: Individual risks and support
items.text: Discuss the treatment aim, injection discomfort and possible nerve injury, bleeding or bruising, liver effects, flushes, joint symptoms and fatigue. Liver impairment or an existing modified dose requires an agreed prescriber and pharmacy plan. Where relevant, use effective contraception during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded. Tell staff about blood thinners; do not stop them yourself.

chapters.title: Checks throughout treatment
chapters.intro: Your team arranges tests and explains the results. A planned check is not confirmation that it has been completed.

items.title: Treatment-specific checks
items.text: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, the menopausal and treatment history, pregnancy exclusion and bleeding risk. Before injections, tell staff about anticoagulants, bruising, bleeding or previous nerve symptoms. Repeat liver tests when indicated; scans follow the agreed cancer-control plan. Tell anyone ordering an oestrogen blood test that you receive fulvestrant because some tests can give a misleadingly high result.

items.title: Heart checks
items.text: ECG or other heart tests depend on symptoms and personal risk; this medicine alone does not require a routine HER2-style echocardiogram schedule.

items.title: Bone health
items.text: Assess personal fracture and osteoporosis risk. Fulvestrant does not carry an automatic AI DXA timetable; agree testing and repeat intervals when indicated.

chapters.title: Your setting changes the pathway
chapters.intro: Choose the pathway that your team has confirmed; these are not all extra treatments you must have.

items.title: Advanced-disease scans
items.text: For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.

items.title: Tumour markers
items.text: Tumour markers may supplement imaging and clinical assessment in advanced disease if they are informative, especially if elevated at baseline. They do not replace scans, and a marker change alone should not determine treatment failure. There is no universal fixed marker timetable.

items.title: Menopause, pregnancy and contraception
items.text: Where relevant, effective contraception is needed during treatment and for two years after the final dose under the EMA product information. Pregnancy and breastfeeding are excluded.

questions.a: The usual schedule is Day 1, Day 15 and Day 29, then every 28 days. The first month includes an extra loading visit. Follow your clinic appointments; contact the team if a visit is missed.

questions.q: When are bloods, ECGs or echoes needed?
questions.a: Before treatment, check blood count, kidney and liver function, the menopausal and treatment history, pregnancy exclusion and bleeding risk. Before injections, tell staff about anticoagulants, bruising, bleeding or previous nerve symptoms. Repeat liver tests when indicated; scans follow the agreed cancer-control plan. Tell anyone ordering an oestrogen blood test that you receive fulvestrant because some tests can give a misleadingly high result. There is no routine ECG or echo schedule for fulvestrant alone; a companion medicine may need additional checks.

For advanced breast cancer, response assessment is generally every two to four months, adapted to disease pace, sites, symptoms and treatment. Indolent disease may be reviewed less often; new symptoms can prompt earlier scans. The team chooses the imaging method; this is not a universal three-month CT chest/abdomen/pelvis order.
Assess personal fracture and osteoporosis risk. Fulvestrant does not carry an automatic AI DXA timetable; agree testing and repeat intervals when indicated.
Continue while the treatment is beneficial and tolerated, with planned response reviews. There is no fixed adjuvant five-year course on this card.

questions.q: Do I need a port or home pump?
questions.a: No port or home infusion pump is needed for this medicine itself. Any separately prescribed medicine has its own access requirements.

questions.q: Is this the same plan as capivasertib with fulvestrant?
questions.a: No. The injections are part of both plans, but capivasertib adds its own tablet schedule, selection requirements, blood-sugar checks and side-effect care. Use the full combination plan if both are prescribed.

questions.q: Why might an oestrogen test need checking?
questions.a: Fulvestrant can interfere with some laboratory tests and make the result look higher than it is. Tell the team about treatment so they can check the test method before making a treatment decision.
